HTTP caching headers

Cache-Control is the only caching header that matters in practice. Expires is a fallback for proxies old enough to be a museum piece, and Pragma has not meant anything useful for two decades.

The interesting pair is max-age and stale-while-revalidate. Together they let a cache serve a slightly old response immediately and refresh it in the background, which turns a cache miss from a latency spike into a background job.

ETags are cheap to add and expensive to get right behind more than one origin server, because two servers computing different ETags for identical content defeat the whole mechanism.
